parallel.requirements: The run recognized the benchmark as a clean-room reverse-engineering task: implement a new richgo-compatible executable from observed CLI behavior and README documentation without inspecting or wrapping the original binary.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent chose a research-first swarm plan, delegating seven behavior domains to explore agents, then keeping implementation, differential testing, and final compile steps assigned to the parent as pending todos.
parallel.implementation: No original source code, build script, or replacement executable was produced; work remained in behavioral probing and partial rule synthesis.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: There were no independently implemented components to integrate, and the submitted artifact remained the initial workspace skeleton with README, LICENSE, .git metadata, and the provided executable.
parallel.verification: The run performed many behavioral probes of the reference executable but never verified a produced clone because no clone was built.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Implementation, differential testing, compile.sh, and final assembly remained unfinished when the second probe swarm was cancelled.

serial.requirements: The serial attempt recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering obligation and the same restrictions against source lookup, binary analysis, wrapping, or reuse.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single agent directly probed line rendering, config, edge cases, and test subcommand behavior while keeping implementation and differential testing as later todo items.
serial.implementation: No replacement source tree or compile script was written; the attempt stayed in manual probing and design notes.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No implementation pieces existed to integrate, and the submitted artifact was the same initial skeleton with no compilable reimplementation.
serial.verification: The agent verified behavior of the reference binary during probes but had no generated implementation to compile or compare.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Implementation and differential testing were still pending at cancellation, so the official evaluator could not compile a solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the clean-room executable reimplementation objective and the prohibition on source lookup, binary inspection, and wrapping.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and followed the same prompt constraints and worked from normal execution and README behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; both failed before producing a required new implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed behavior discovery across a first seven-agent swarm and retained implementation as a later parent-owned todo.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation and tracked all probes and later implementation inside one local todo list.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created overlapping investigators but sequenced productive implementation after the probe phase; serial had no child ownership boundary but also delayed implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The first child reports were returned to the parent, which then recorded a todo to read them and still had implementation pending before launching more probes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained probe findings locally and updated its own todo state, with config and test behavior still in progress and implementation pending.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main contrast is not lost or conflicting context; it is that parallel converted returned context into another investigation wave instead of implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not create replacement source or compile machinery; the final artifact list lacks implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise did not create replacement source or compile machinery; the artifact list is the same skeleton.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation paths terminated before coding, so the official compile failure has the same immediate artifact cause.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The first swarm completed, but a second detail-probing swarm was still active when the run cancellation occurred.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to join; the sole process was cancelled while local probing tasks remained in progress.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result lifecycle event: new investigator results were prevented by cancellation; serial had only local incomplete work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No implementation writes by multiple agents were integrated or collided; the final tree retained only the initial files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no shared workspace coordination and no implementation writes to integrate.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no shared-state or merge divergence; both lacked deliverable assembly rather than suffering write conflicts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified reference behavior through probes but never ran acceptance on a replacement and officially failed compile.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also probed reference behavior but never ran acceptance on a produced replacement and officially failed compile.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The verification outcome is the same: no clone-level validation existed, and both official evaluations stopped at compile_failed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the run on two waves of behavior investigation and was cancelled while the second wave was active.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed the run on direct probing and was cancelled with implementation still pending.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's concurrency-specific budget problem was the second research wave after first results; serial had ordinary single-stream probe overrun.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. The current completed status.json evaluation for both modes reports compile_failed, solution_passed false, and 787 tests not run. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel used child swarms and deferred implementation behind investigation, while serial performed the investigation locally. Both final artifacts lacked a compilable clean-room implementation.
parallel_contributors: Parallel launched a second investigation swarm after first-wave findings and before implementation or assembly.
serial_contributors: Serial continued direct probing until cancellation and also did not reach implementation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Neither run produced implementation code, so there are no ordinary code-level differences to compare.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized adverse parallel process consequence only.

candidates.reason: Implementation was explicitly tracked as a parent todo, so the problem was not absent ownership.
No separate component implementations were produced, so there was no concrete unowned integration step.
Final assembly was listed as pending, and the blocking failure was never reaching implementation rather than missing assembly ownership.
The parent held the end-to-end todo chain, but investigation scheduling consumed the run before the pipeline advanced.
There was no single mandatory preflight, harness, or oracle gate; the visible gate was an extended multi-agent investigation phase.
Parallel investigators overlapped, but implementation stayed deferred after the first research wave and the parent launched a second probe swarm before any buildable clone was created.
candidates.realized_consequence: Implementation and final assembly were displaced behind continued investigation, and the submitted parallel artifact contained no compilable reimplementation.
candidates.near_match_reason: Fan-out consumed time, but the more specific boundary was that all productive implementation remained after a serial investigation phase and a second probe wave.

candidates.reason: The indispensable implementation path started too late because investigation stayed serially phased; Serial Investigation is the more specific boundary.
The run had broad fan-out, but the retained issue is the second research phase deferring implementation, not child count alone exhausting budget.
No single child had a uniquely overbroad implementation-critical assignment that independently left required work unfinished.
The child briefs included clean-room constraints and specific probe scopes; no child work became unusable due to an omitted known requirement.
The delegated children were behavior investigators, not separate component implementers expected to interoperate through an omitted contract.
No specific known finding disappeared during transfer and caused repeated work or a wrong implementation action.
The first swarm reports were large, but the evidence shows the parent chose more probes rather than being unable to reduce a returned handoff.
No child result described superseded workspace or requirement state that the parent then consumed incorrectly.
No incompatible child reports or contracts remained unadjudicated at an implementation or integration decision point.
The parent never claimed or presented a completed whole-task solution; the run ended by cancellation before implementation.
The second probe wave asked for additional details, not a replacement retry that repeated prior work without inherited findings.

candidates.reason: Second-wave children were aborted by the overall run cancellation, but that is downstream of the retained serial investigation chain.
No complete candidate or compatible component set existed for promotion or packaging before closure.
There was no implementation merge and no prior integrated verification pass that a later merge invalidated.
No child completed a delegated implementation that the parent could have retrieved or joined.
The active children were investigators rather than verifiers with completed concrete findings trapped below the parent.
The visible child abort came with whole-run cancellation, leaving no separate parent decision window for takeover.
The first-wave results were returned and incorporated into the parent planning state; no completed result was visibly ignored.
The parent did not simply wait blindly; it actively launched and managed probe work until cancellation.
No concurrent agents wrote competing implementation files or overlapping behavior claims into the workspace.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file and observed a conflicting change.
No non-entry source created or owned by another agent was replaced, deleted, or rewritten.
The required submitted executable or entry-point source was not concurrently replaced or overwritten.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple final workspace outputs from another actor.
There were no multiple live implementation writers causing unstable shared state or provenance problems.
No generated file, fixture, cache, temporary path, or tool from one concurrent actor was consumed as stable input by another.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel run used overlapping investigators, but kept implementation as a later phase after returned research and then launched a second probe swarm; cancellation arrived before implementation or final assembly.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: A buildable richgo clone was never produced because implementation and final assembly were left after the parallel investigation phase.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The second wave contributed to budget pressure, but the correction would be starting implementation after the first investigative handoff rather than merely reducing child count.
